resources.string: Measure the power going into the battery as it charges.
Charger connected. Power drawn from the battery cannot be measured. Tap for the charge test.
Waiting for readings that identify the battery current.
The charger is connected. No power is reaching the battery right now.
Measuring what the phone draws from the battery. Leave the charger disconnected for 20 seconds.
The test starts as soon as the phone detects the charger.
This is what reaches the battery. The charger also powers the phone and covers losses in the charging circuit, which this test cannot measure.
Leave the phone idle. Using it during the test changes the measurement.
Power and battery temperature over time
There are no readings for this chart yet.
The charge test ended, but the result could not be saved.
This phone cannot measure charging power. The battery current or voltage is unavailable or cannot be interpreted.
A dash means the phone could not give that reading.
The battery has reached 45 °C. The test stops at 47 °C.
The battery got too hot. Unplug the charger to stop charging.
A dash means there were too few readings or the condition was not observed.
This setup delivered up to %1$s to the battery, typical of a computer USB port.
This setup delivered up to %1$s to the battery, typical of standard 5–10 W charging.
This setup delivered up to %1$s to the battery. Fast charging was active.
This setup delivered up to %1$s to the battery. High-power fast charging was active.
Power dropped as the battery passed 40 °C. Heat may have slowed charging.
The test started above 80%, where the phone already slows charging. For a comparison, start between 20% and 50%.
The current reading changed about every %1$s s. Short peaks may be missed.
Compare two charge tests to check a charger or cable. Load tests measure power drawn from the battery, in the opposite direction.
Compare the curves at the same battery percentage.
